statement: Individually identifiable health information is a subset of health information that is created or received by a health care provider, health plan, employer or clearinghouse, relates to the past, present or future health or condition of an individual, the provision of health care to an individual, or the past, present or future payment for that care, and identifies the individual or gives a reasonable basis to believe it can identify the individual. Protected health information is individually identifiable health information that is transmitted or maintained in electronic or other form (with listed exclusions).
location: 45 CFR 160.103, definitions of individually identifiable health information and protected health information
inference: Health status alone is not the trigger: the information must relate to health, care or payment for care AND identify an individual, and it must be held by a listed holder type. A bare structured value is therefore phi only when a health, care or payment relationship and a holder are both present; an identifier next to a patient label is a candidate, not an established case. Payment for care brings billing records within scope when the payer or provider relationship is health-related.

notes: Read from a mirror of the regulation, not the eCFR page itself.
The definition's exclusion paragraphs (education records, employment records held as employer) were not worked through; they bear on employer-held and customer-held data.
uncertainty.wouldSettle: Read the eCFR text and HHS guidance on employment records and on non-covered holders.

statement: Health information that does not identify an individual, and with respect to which there is no reasonable basis to believe it can be used to identify an individual, is not individually identifiable health information (paragraph (a)).
inference: Identification of an individual is part of the test, so a value that cannot reach any individual (a reserved or never-assigned value) is outside the protected set by the regulation's own logic. This is project inference: the regulation addresses information, not tokens, and it does not discuss test values.

notes: Read from a mirror of the regulation; the application to reserved or documentation values is project inference, not source-stated.
uncertainty.wouldSettle: HHS guidance that addresses test or example values, if any exists.

statement: Social security numbers (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(G)) and account numbers (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(J)) are listed among the identifiers that must be removed for the safe-harbor de-identification method.
inference: An SSN, and an account number such as a payment card or bank account tied to a patient's care, belong to the same identifier list as email and telephone, so the same contextual composition (base kind plus medical or health-plan context) applies. The list does not name payment cards or IBANs; reading them as account numbers is project inference.

notes: Read from a mirror of the regulation.
Whether a payment card or IBAN is an account number in the regulation's sense is not source-stated.
uncertainty.wouldSettle: HHS guidance that addresses payment cards and bank account numbers in health billing.
